question: Why can death never again apply to one who has already died in realization?
premises: The subject is described as already dead
Death is denied for that subject
The denial is made absolute by not ever
inference: For one who has truly died, death does not exist at any time.
uncertainties: Whether mṛtasya refers to physical or ego-death is context-dependent
plain_english: For one who is dead, there is indeed no death ever again.
